Basically, I'm moving from a large city to just outside of it on a small farm. The farm there has goats and chickens and did have a horse, but the horse sadly passed away last week (she was 25 years old, RIP Crystal). The previous owners are moving halfway across the country and asked us to keep the goats and chickens. At first, we were really hesitant. We've lived in the city all out lives and the idea of keeping goats was a little scary. The only animals I've ever had were mice, fish, and cats, and I'd never been able to keep the cats from eating my mice and fish.

The owners started looking at other options and found a lady that was willing to take all seven of them in. They were desperate, so they agreed, and the woman picked them up. The previous owners seriously love their animals. They're devastated to leave them behind, but they're moving somewhere they know the goats won't be happy. The wife decided she wanted to check in on her goats and make sure they liked it in their new home, but holy shit when they got there, she said she started bawling.

The woman was a hillbilly obeast. She also hoarded animals. The wife said she must have had over 40 rabbits, and a few were dead in the cages with the rest of the rabbits. There were cats and dogs forced into kennels with too many other animals, sleeping in their own poop and food. The goats were kept separate from each other in cages they couldn't even turn around in. In the group of seven there were two 1-year-olds, Partner and Rascal. Rascal is a few months younger and is still seriously attached to his mother, Nina. Partner was a runt and was rejected by his mother, Bonnie, and was raised by the husband instead. He's the sweetest little thing and follows you around everywhere, bleating the entire time, but he also needs a lot of human attention, because the others kind of exclude him still.

The owner was, of course, pissed. She managed to get four of the seven goats out of there, but the woman started threatening her, and she had to leave three behind. We are calling the police, but in order to make sure my family gets the goats, we have to wait until we're moved in so we'll be the ones to adopt them, that way they'll be with the others again.

They are the sweetest animals ever. Bonnie and Billy are like an old married couple. She likes to put her head on my lap when I'm visiting and just let me pet her, and Billy will walk over to her and start rubbing his head on her. If you stop petting her she starts to rub her little horns on your leg or gnaws on your thumb a bit (not painfully, none of them bite hard). Little Partner just follows me everywhere and will try to jump on you to get your attention. Rascal is still scared of me, but he's let me pet him a couple of times. Nina is extremely shy, but she eats the grass I offer, so we have a quiet kind of friendship. I also found out that Nina and Bonnie might be pregnant, and the idea of them going through that while they've got buns in the oven makes me want to vomit.

Just the idea that someone could do that to these sweet animals horrifies me. Billy was really fluffy and huge looking when I first saw him. The owners used him for breeding, and he was gorgeous, but by the time he came back he was balding and already losing weight.

I didn't realize I could hate obeasts more. I just really needed to get this off my chest after visiting all the goats again today. The wife was honestly beating herself up so much and blamed herself for putting her goats through that. To go from having the horse you've had for 12 years dying to finding out the goats you've had for almost as long were abused by the woman you gave them to, I couldn't imagine it.
